findings.title: Concurrent-deletion NPE is still reachable through the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix only makes getSubGroupsCount() tolerate modelSupplier.get() returning null. The neighbouring overrides getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` and dereference the result without a null check. When a CachedGroup is read while its row has been deleted concurrently - the exact scenario this PR targets - the delegate returned by modelSupplier is null, so calling these methods on the cached adapter (which is what the paginated/filtered subgroup endpoints do) still throws NPE. The fix is therefore incomplete unless the same null handling is applied there (or the model is fetched and null-checked in one place).

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss the exception it is looking for
findings.body: The reader thread is started and never joined: the main thread deletes the 100 groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty (line 157). Any read request that is still in flight when the last group is deleted - precisely the window in which the NPE occurs - can add its exception to the list after the assertion has already run, so the test can pass even though the bug is present and is inherently racy. In addition, if a remove() call throws before deletedAll is set, this non-daemon thread loops forever, continuing to issue admin requests into subsequent tests and potentially hanging the JVM. The loop should be wrapped in try/finally, the flag set in the finally block, and the thread joined (with a timeout) before asserting.

findings.title: Test never requests subgroup counts, so the method changed by this PR may not be exercised
findings.body: The reader calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, which only fills in search/first/max/briefRepresentation. Subgroup counts are populated only when the request opts into them (the subGroupCount request parameter that leads to GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount), and with briefRepresentation=true and no such flag the server never calls GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() - the method this PR modifies. If so, the test would pass on the unfixed code and provides no regression coverage. The read request should explicitly ask for subgroup counts (e.g. the overload with the subGroupCount parameter) so getSubGroupsCount() is on the request path.

findings.title: Unthrottled reader loop hammers the server for the whole duration of the deletions
findings.body: The background loop has no delay/backoff and repeatedly issues `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` admin requests as fast as the client can go while 100 groups are deleted sequentially. On CI this generates a large burst of concurrent requests (each building a list of up to 100 groups) that can starve the server, cause timeouts and make the test flaky. Add a small sleep/backoff or cap the number of iterations.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null where it previously always returned a count
findings.body: This method previously never returned null (it either produced a count or threw), so callers had no reason to treat the Long as nullable. With the change, a deleted cached group yields null, which will throw NPE for any caller that auto-unboxes the value (comparisons, arithmetic, or passing it to a primitive parameter) and silently drops the count from serialized representations. The nullability should be documented/handled explicitly, and the callers of GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount audited for unboxing assumptions.
